notes.claim: Hydraulic graphical symbols give no information about how a component is built.
A pump and a motor symbol differ only in where the arrow touches the circle: the point for a pump, the tail for a motor.
Fluid power symbols may be rotated or reversed without changing their meaning, except for lines to reservoirs and vented manifolds.

sources.title: Hydraulics Basic Principles - Bosch
sources.quote: Graphic symbols of hydraulics do not provide information about the design structure of the components.

sources.title: Engineering Symbology, Prints, and Drawings, Module 2: Engineering Fluid Diagrams and Prints (DOE-HDBK-1016/1-93)
sources.quote: The difference between them is that the point of the arrow touches the circle in a pump and the tail of the arrow touches the circle in a motor.

sources.title: Basic Diagrams and Systems | Engineering Library (US Navy NAVEDTRA 14105A, Fluid Power, chapter 12)
sources.quote: Symbols may be rotated or reversed without altering their meaning except in cases of lines to reservoirs and vented manifolds
